newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed 200,000 customers lose power.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed 200,000 customers lose power.

text.p: Detroit Edison said Friday more than 200,000 electricity customers lost power late Thursday and early Friday after an ice storm struck southeastern Michigan, pressuring tree limbs on power lines.

"We have all available Detroit Edison employees working on the restoration effort, but we have a lot of hard work ahead of us because of the number of downed lines and the type of damage sustained," Robert Buckler, Detroit Edison's executive vice president said in a statement.
The company could not yet comment on how many transmission lines were down or their size.
"It should be a gradual restoration through the weekend and into early next week," company spokesman Scott Simons said.
He noted that the utility serves more than two million customers in the area.
"We hope to have estimates for when service will be restored to specific areas after 2 p.m. (1400 CST)," Buckler said in the statement.
Nearly 65 crews from Illinois and Indiana utilities are joining in the restoration effort.
Detroit Edison is a subsidiary of DTE Energy Co.
